rules.statement: Do not ship EF Core migrations in a published, reusable persistence library; the library ships only the model, and the consuming host owns the provider-specific migrations.
rules.why: Migrations are provider-specific SQL. Shipping them in the package would tie it to one provider and to each consumer's schema lifecycle and deployment schedule.
rules.check: Look for Migrations folders, Migration classes or ModelSnapshot files added to a packable library project, as opposed to a host or app project.

rules.statement: Never call `Database.Migrate()` or apply schema changes at application startup outside the Development environment; apply them deliberately out-of-band, for example with an idempotent `dotnet ef migrations script --idempotent` script.
rules.why: Schema changes to a shared production database must be deliberate and observable. They should not be a side effect of a rolling deploy, which is unsafe when several instances start at once.
rules.check: Look for `Migrate()`/`MigrateAsync()` calls in startup code that are not guarded by an `IsDevelopment()` check.

rules.statement: Do not use `EnsureCreated()` for a relational database whose schema must evolve; use EF Core migrations, and keep `EnsureCreated()` only for the in-memory provider.
rules.why: `EnsureCreated()` never changes an existing schema, so new entities fail at runtime with missing tables. A database it creates also has no migrations history, so it cannot be migrated later.
rules.check: Look for `EnsureCreated()`/`EnsureCreatedAsync()` calls against relational providers such as SQLite or SQL Server.

rules.statement: Provide an `IDesignTimeDbContextFactory<TContext>` in the project that owns the migrations, and set `MigrationsAssembly` in the runtime DbContext registration to that project.
rules.why: With the factory, `dotnet ef` never boots the full web host, and setting `MigrationsAssembly` lets `Migrate()` find the migrations at runtime.
rules.check: Look for migrations added to a project that has no design-time factory, or for a DbContext registration whose provider options do not set `MigrationsAssembly` when the migrations live outside the context's assembly.

rules.statement: Keep a separate migration set for each database provider; never reuse one provider's migrations on another.
rules.why: Migrations are provider-specific SQL, so a SQLite migration cannot run on SQL Server.
rules.check: Look for a single migrations set applied to several providers, or for a newly supported provider that comes without its own migrations.

rules.statement: When startup finds a relational database that has tables but no applied migrations, fail fast with an actionable message; never delete the database automatically.
rules.why: A clear message is better than a raw provider 'table already exists' error, and deleting the database automatically would lose data.
rules.check: Look for startup database initialization that calls `EnsureDeleted()` automatically, or that lets a migration run into a provider error on a database built by `EnsureCreated()`.

rules.statement: Treat generated EF Core migration files as generated code: exclude them from CSharpier and mark them `generated_code = true` in `.editorconfig`.
rules.why: Generated migrations should not be reformatted or held to the analyzer and warnings-as-errors gates.
rules.check: Look for a new migrations folder that has no `.csharpierignore` entry and no `generated_code` editorconfig setting, or for manual reformatting of migration files.
